_comment: Which radar and moment each ramp was measured against, and what the
measurement found. The registry answers only for pairs listed here, so a
ramp cannot reach a legend or a readout without this evidence.
Produced by validation_tests/visual/ramp_coverage.py, which samples every
distinct opaque color in real frames and asks the shipped invert.ts what
each one reads as. 'colors' is matched over distinct; a ramp ships only at
'radar' is the id the app holds, as RADAR_FOLDER in backend/config.py keys
it, and 'folder' is where the frames were read from. 'moment' is the
published prefix, which is what moment_to_prefix() resolves a console
Adding a pair means running the tool and pasting its numbers, not editing

KBBX, KDAX and KMUX publish a reflectivity bar in the same tree (md5 aad5def3, -30 to 80 dBZ, measured 15/15 over 422,055 px on 2026-07-01 frames). It is left out because the console never paints those frames: they are not selectable radars, and the NEXRAD overlay draws the Iowa State nexrad-n0q-wmst WMS layer, which uses the NWS N0Q ramp instead. A ramp with no display path is one more thing to mistake for the right one.

These rows measure colors, which cannot detect a shift of the scale. The aqpi-xband-reflectivity rows matched at 100% on 2026-11-21 against a ramp read off the bar, 22 linear bins over -20 to 80, and that ramp was wrong by up to 9.5 dBZ: the frames are painted through BoundaryNorm(-25..75 by 5, extend both) and the bar is not. On 2026-11-23 the ramp was rebuilt from the plotting code by build_boundary_ramps.py, with the same 22 colors, so these rows stand for the colors and the code reading stands for the range.

pairs.note: The C-band paints ZDR from its own colormap, which is why it read 0 of 253 against the X-band table. Its renderer gives from_list("zdr", 13 anchors, N=256) over Normalize(-1, 5), where the X-band uses HomeyerRainbow over (-2, 4), so both the map and the range differ. Read from c_band_plotting.py on the C-band producer host 2026-11-21 and measured here at 253/253. The 253 is the count the renderer's own colormap collapses to, and it is the same 253 the earlier rejection reported, which is what confirms this is the right source. sscb still publishes no colorbar; the table came from the code.

Its own colormap, like the C-band's ZDR: from_list("phidp_grad", 10 colors, N=256) over Normalize(-180, 180), against the X-band's HomeyerRainbow over the same range. Read from c_band_plotting.py on the C-band producer host 2026-11-21 and measured at 256/256, the same 256 the earlier rejection counted. The renderer writes the colors at explicit positions, which come out uniform at k/9 because its value array steps by 40 the whole way across, so the stored ramp is the plain uniform list; the two forms were compared over all 256 triples. Its prefix is PhiDP rather than FilteredPhiDP, unfiltered, which moment_to_prefix() already special-cases.

Measured 2026-11-21 over the ten newest scans. The console opens on this radar and this moment, and it had no measured pair, so the legend and the readout were off on the view the console opens in. Thin frames on a quiet day: 740 opaque pixels carrying 15 of the palette's 17 colors. The palette itself is the band's, established by XEBY and XSCR at 17/17 over 184,158 pixels.
Measured 2026-11-21 over the ten newest scans.
Measured 2026-11-21 over the ten newest scans.

Measured 2026-11-21 over a frame with rain across most of the scan, which is why it reaches 211 of the palette's 56 stops' worth of quantised colors. These four pairs could not be measured before today: the scan route handed every moment a filesystem fetcher on a deployment with no mount, so Velocity, Zdr and PhiDP answered 500 and only Reflectivity, which the archive already held, came back at all.

Measured 2026-11-21 on a nearly clear scan: 74 opaque pixels carrying 17 colors, so this exercises a small part of the table. The table itself is the band's, established by XSCW at 211/211 over 133,663 pixels off a byte-identical colorbar.
Measured 2026-11-21 on a nearly clear scan, 57 opaque pixels. The table is established by XSCW at 235/235 over 133,663 pixels off a byte-identical colorbar.
Measured 2026-11-21 on a nearly clear scan, 74 opaque pixels. The table is established by XSCW as above.

Measured 2026-11-22 against three frames from 2026-11-19 read off the dated tree on the AQPI deployment, since the scan route serves only a rolling hour and this radar's filtered PhiDP is transparent through all of it on a quiet day. 87 colors over 351,204 pixels, which is the fullest exercise this ramp has had on any radar. A 2026-04-16 frame from the same tree reads 0 of 48: the renderer's PhiDP colormap changed between April and November, and the colorbar on disk changed with it, from d694c2c4 to today's f75aab2c. The shipped ramp is built from the current bar, so it reads current frames and refuses older ones, which fails safe rather than quietly: an unmatched color reports 'not on this scale' instead of a wrong number.

Measured 2026-11-22 against frames from 2026-11-13, 11-18 and 11-19 read off the dated tree on the AQPI deployment, for the same reason as XSCV above: the scan route serves a rolling hour and this radar's filtered PhiDP is transparent through all of it on a quiet day. 69 colors over 867,370 pixels. Every X-band pair is now measured on frames and none rests on its colorbar alone.

The only radar that publishes RhoHV at all: the five X-band folders carry Reflectivity, Zdr, FilteredPhiDP and Velocity, and the route answers 404 for RhoHV on every one of them. Plain matplotlib viridis over Normalize(0.0, 1.0), with both bounds literal in c_band_plotting.py on the C-band producer host rather than taken from the 0-to-1 convention, which is what makes the scale a reading instead of a guess. Measured at 254/254, and 254 is viridis's own distinct count out of 256 entries. The frame is 2.9 MB against 0.2 to 0.6 for the others because the renderer applies its (ncp > 0.7) and (snr > 5) mask to dbz, zdr, vel and phidp and writes rhohv raw, so the speckle is the data.

shared_colorbars._comment: Radars whose colorbar PNGs are byte-identical to the measured one, so they paint from the same table. md5 prefixes read on 2026-11-21. The C-band publishes no colorbar and so appears nowhere here, however its frames are measured above.
